Subject: High latency observed for Zephyr Analytics (9:05 PDT spike)

Team —

We started seeing a sustained latency increase for the Zephyr Analytics tenant beginning ~09:05 PDT. P95 jumped from ~210ms to ~1.8s for generation endpoints; throughput dropped ~25% as backpressure kicked in. Error rate stayed low (0.3% 5xx), so not an immediate crash but poor customer experience.

Quick notes:
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (model: rwk-13B-v1)
- Regions impacted: us-west-2 primary; failover region (us-east-1) healthy
- Recent infra change: kernel selection push at 08:40 PDT to optimize long-seq workloads (rollout 50%)

Attaching a couple of graphs (latency-graphs-2026-04-02.png). Opening an incident: INC-4921.

Immediate ask: SRE needs stakeholder direction for temporary mitigations (rollback, routing, model fallback). Waiting on product decision re: customer messaging.

Diego

Quick triage from eng:
- We rolled a kernel selection tweak at 08:40 that changes attention kernel selection heuristics for long sequences. The canary in us-east-1 wasn't hit by similar long-seq traffic, which explains the regional delta.
- Fastest mitigations in order (ETA):
  1) Route Zephyr traffic to us-east-1 via routing policy override (~7-10m to flip and validate).
  2) Apply model fallback to rwk-7B (config flag) for the Zephyr tenant (~10-15m, immediate CPU/GPU resource check needed).
  3) Roll back kernel change entirely (~20-30m plus monitoring).

I recommend routing to us-east-1 first to get the customer responsive while we evaluate patch complexity. I'll start the routing override now if Diego/Hannah confirm network/regulatory ok.

Sean

Update from SRE ops:
- We routed Zephyr traffic to us-east-1 at 10:12 PDT. Observed p95 fall from ~1.8s -> ~230ms across the next 18 minutes. Throughput recovered to 98% baseline.
- Applied model fallback to rwk-7B as a precaution for a small subset (10% of traffic) at 10:35 PDT; no adverse effects observed.
- Kernel rollback is on standby if anomalous behaviors reappear.

I've attached the mitigation-checklist.md that documents the steps we took. We're keeping the routing override in place while Eng completes a targeted rollback candidate and tests it in a staging canary.

Action items:
- Product: evaluate whether we should gate kernel selection changes by tenant-level canaries.
- CS: send the draft to Tom/Linh now (Marissa).
- Eng: publish RCA plan and timeline; propose a fix-and-rollback window.

Subject: Product asks & roadmap questions after Zephyr incident

Folks — following yesterday's incident and Hannah's mitigation summary, I'm putting forward a short set of product asks to take to planning: 

1) Tenant-level canary controls for kernel rollout (config toggle + automatic rollback window). This prevents single-tenant regressions.
2) Per-tenant routing policy overrides: make the routing override a first-class API so CS can flip with guardrails.
3) Model-fallback policy: formalize rules for automatic fallback to cheaper/older variants when latency > threshold for X minutes.
4) Prioritize a postmortem + RCA in the next 72 hours and schedule a hotfix sprint if the kernel change is root-cause.

Soojin/Markus — need your sign-off to create a short-term roadmap ticket and request an exception to the normal planning cadence to accelerate these items (I estimate ~2 sprint points per item, except #4 which is ops-driven).

Maya
